ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

payload.proof_nl:
Proof.

If m = 1, then t is empty. There is exactly one permutation of {1}, namely (1), and it satisfies the vacuous sign conditions, so U_1(t) = 1. Also Peak(t) = {1}, t^{<1} and t^{>1} are empty, and the right-hand side is binom(0,0) U_0(empty) U_0(empty) = 1. So the identity holds.

Now assume m >= 2. Let S be the set of permutations b = (b_1,...,b_m) of {1,...,m} such that t_i (b_{i+1} - b_i) > 0 for all 1 <= i <= m-1. Then |S| = U_m(t).

For each j with 1 <= j <= m, let S_j = { b in S : b_j = m }. Since every permutation of {1,...,m} contains m in exactly one position, the sets S_1,...,S_m are disjoint and their union is S. Hence
U_m(t) = sum from j=1 to m of |S_j|.

We first determine when S_j can be nonempty.

1. If j = 1 and b is in S_1, then b_2 - b_1 = b_2 - m < 0. Since t_1 (b_2 - m) > 0, necessarily t_1 = -1. Thus 1 is in Peak(t).

2. If j = m and b is in S_m, then b_m - b_{m-1} = m - b_{m-1} > 0. Since t_{m-1} (m - b_{m-1}) > 0, necessarily t_{m-1} = +1. Thus m is in Peak(t).

3. If 2 <= j <= m-1 and b is in S_j, then m - b_{j-1} > 0 and b_{j+1} - m < 0. The conditions at indices j-1 and j give
t_{j-1} (m - b_{j-1}) > 0 and t_j (b_{j+1} - m) > 0,
so necessarily t_{j-1} = +1 and t_j = -1. Thus j is in Peak(t).

Therefore S_j is empty whenever j is not in Peak(t).

Now fix j in Peak(t). We count S_j.

For b in S_j, let A = {b_1,...,b_{j-1}}, the set of values appearing to the left of m. Then A is a subset of {1,...,m-1} with size j-1. Conversely, any subset A of {1,...,m-1} with size j-1 can serve as the left value-set. There are binom(m-1,j-1) choices for A. Once A is fixed, the set B = {1,...,m-1} minus A is forced; it has size m-j and is the set of values to the right of m.

We now count, for fixed A, the possible left block (b_1,...,b_{j-1}).

If j = 1, there is no left block, so there is exactly one possibility, and this equals U_0(empty) by definition.

Assume j > 1. Write A = {a_1 < a_2 < ... < a_{j-1}}. Any ordering of A is uniquely of the form
(a_{c_1},...,a_{c_{j-1}})
for some permutation c = (c_1,...,c_{j-1}) of {1,...,j-1}. For each i with 1 <= i <= j-2, because the map k -> a_k is strictly increasing, we have
a_{c_{i+1}} > a_{c_i} exactly when c_{i+1} > c_i,
and
a_{c_{i+1}} < a_{c_i} exactly when c_{i+1} < c_i.
So the sign of a_{c_{i+1}} - a_{c_i} is the same as the sign of c_{i+1} - c_i. Therefore
t_i (a_{c_{i+1}} - a_{c_i}) > 0 exactly when t_i (c_{i+1} - c_i) > 0.
Hence the number of left blocks using exactly the set A and satisfying the sign conditions at indices 1,...,j-2 is exactly U_{j-1}(t^{<j}), since t^{<j} = (t_1,...,t_{j-2}).

Similarly, for the fixed set B, the number of possible right blocks (b_{j+1},...,b_m) satisfying the sign conditions at indices j+1,...,m-1 is exactly U_{m-j}(t^{>j}), because t^{>j} = (t_{j+1},...,t_{m-1}) and the same increasing-relabeling argument applies. If j = m, there is no right block, and this number is U_0(empty) = 1.

It remains to check the sign conditions involving the entry m itself. Since j is in Peak(t), these are automatic:
- if j > 1, then t_{j-1} = +1, and because b_{j-1} < m we have t_{j-1} (m - b_{j-1}) > 0;
- if j < m, then t_j = -1, and because b_{j+1} < m we have t_j (b_{j+1} - m) > 0.

So, once A is fixed, every valid left block and every valid right block combine uniquely with m in position j to form an element of S_j, and every element of S_j arises uniquely in this way. Therefore
|S_j| = binom(m-1,j-1) U_{j-1}(t^{<j}) U_{m-j}(t^{>j}).

Since |S_j| = 0 for j not in Peak(t), we conclude that
U_m(t) = sum over j in Peak(t) of binom(m-1,j-1) U_{j-1}(t^{<j}) U_{m-j}(t^{>j}).
This is exactly the claimed identity.

domain_restrictions: m is an integer and m is at least 1.
t is a sign sequence of length m minus 1, with each entry equal to plus 1 or minus 1.
When m equals 1, the sequence t is empty and Peak(t) is exactly the set containing 1.
r is an integer and r is at least 0.
When r is 0, the sign sequence u is empty and U_0 of the empty sequence is defined to be 1.
When r is at least 1, u has length r minus 1 and the counted object is a permutation of 1 through r.
The defining inequalities for U_r(u) require all indices i from 1 to r minus 1.

For Peak(t) with m at least 2, 1 is a peak exactly when t_1 equals minus 1, m is a peak exactly when t_{m minus 1} equals plus 1, and interior j are peaks exactly when the left sign is plus 1 and the right sign is minus 1.
For each j from 1 to m, t left of j means the prefix ending at index j minus 2, and t right of j means the suffix starting at index j plus 1; either is empty if the indicated index range is invalid.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer m at least 1 and every sign sequence t of length m minus 1, the quantity U_m of t equals the sum over all peak positions j in Peak(t) of binomial coefficient m minus 1 choose j minus 1 times U_{j minus 1} of the left truncated sign sequence times U_{m minus j} of the right truncated sign sequence.
quantifier_order: For every integer m at least 1, choose a sign sequence t of length m minus 1 with entries plus 1 or minus 1.
For every integer r at least 0 and every compatible sign sequence u, define U_r(u) by counting permutations of 1 through r that satisfy the sign inequalities.
For every integer j from 1 to m, define the truncated sequences t left of j and t right of j, and define membership in Peak(t) from the neighboring signs.
Then the identity U_m(t) equals the sum over j in Peak(t) of the stated product holds.

payload.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 1, and let t = (t_1,...,t_{m-1}) be a sign sequence with each t_i in {+1,-1}; when m = 1 this sequence is empty. For an integer r >= 0 and a sign sequence u of length r-1 when r >= 1 (and u empty when r = 0), define U_r(u) to be the number of permutations (b_1,...,b_r) of {1,...,r} satisfying u_i * (b_{i+1} - b_i) > 0 for all 1 <= i <= r-1, and set U_0(empty) = 1. Define Peak(t) subseteq {1,...,m} by: if m = 1 then Peak(t) = {1}; if m >= 2 then 1 belongs to Peak(t) exactly when t_1 = -1, m belongs to Peak(t) exactly when t_{m-1} = +1, and for each integer j with 2 <= j <= m-1, j belongs to Peak(t) exactly when t_{j-1} = +1 and t_j = -1. For each integer j with 1 <= j <= m, define t^{<j} = (t_1,...,t_{j-2}) and t^{>j} = (t_{j+1},...,t_{m-1}), interpreting these as the empty sequence when the lower index exceeds the upper. Then U_m(t) = sum over j in Peak(t) of binom(m-1, j-1) * U_{j-1}(t^{<j}) * U_{m-j}(t^{>j}).
